From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodelabs.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodelabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodelabs.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — inference flight and next steps

Hi Priya — great to meet you and Sam today. Quick written recap below and a 3-test POC plan attached. Ben and Neha are looped in for cost + procurement details.

Summary (short): Redwood offers a unified runtime that reduces per-token cost via batching + prefix/KV cache. For the config you listed (100ms p95 target, batching window 20ms, cache hit ~30%), we expect single-region per-1M token costs materially lower than hyperscaler-hosted managed endpoints because of continuous batching and cache reuse. See the attached spreadsheet for the detailed model.

Key constraints / notes:
- KV cache: soft limits depend on instance class; for our typical 8xA100-like pool we allocate 24GB per instance to KV cache; eviction is LRU by prefix and TTL (configurable).
- Batching: continuous batching reduces overhead at high QPS; 20ms batching is reasonable for your latency target but throughput and batch fill depend on real request skew.
- Fallbacks: if dedicated capacity is constrained, we can fall back to a smaller quantized variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost.

Attachments sent: redwood-cost-breakdown-1Mtokens.xlsx (detailed model), redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (deployment/network), acme-security-questions.pdf (we annotated your list).

Proposed 3-test POC plan (high level):
1) Baseline comparison: run 1M tokens through your current hyperscaler endpoint and our hosted Redwood API, collect p50/p95, mean cost, token breakdown.
2) Batching sweep: vary batching windows (10/20/50ms) and measure effective per-token cost and p95.
3) Cache experiment: seed prefix cache for top 500 queries and measure cache hit rate sensitivity (10/30/50% hit).

Requested from Acme: sample production-like prompt set (~5k prompts), expected QPS profile (per-minute distribution), and a security contact for SOC2 artifacts.

Next steps: I’ll circulate the cost spreadsheet and propose calendar slots for the POC runbook sync. If that works, can we schedule the kickoff for next Wednesday (Mar 17)?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodelabs.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodelabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodelabs.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick cost sketch vs hyperscalers (for Acme)

Rachel / Neha — I ran a quick sketch from the demo numbers and want to share a concise competitor comparison to bring into the POC kickoff. High-level assumptions (matches Priya’s ask):
- Traffic: 2 concurrent clients, steady-state 40 rps peak, 20ms batching window; 1M tokens test
- Model: 8k context transformer (approx 45B param equivalent)
- Cache: 30% hit baseline, LRU eviction

Estimated unit economics (per-1M tokens):
- Redwood (hosted, optimized batching + KV cache): $340 per 1M tokens (assumes 30% cache hit, quantization not used)
- AWS managed endpoint: $560 per 1M tokens (higher baseline request overhead, lower caching)
- GCP Vertex AI: $610 per 1M tokens (higher GPU-hour allocation; default lower batching)
- Self-hosted tuned (on comparable infra): $300 per 1M tokens but with engineering ops burden and 3-6 months OPEX ramp to reach stability

Notes: the biggest levers are batching window and cache hit. If we can get to 50% cache hit via prefix strategies, Redwood drops to ~$250 per 1M tokens in this model. Also note that hyperscalers often charge egress or extra model conversion fees which we can surface in procurement.

Action items for POC doc (internal):
- Prepare the cost spreadsheet with cell-level assumptions and inputs (I attached redwood-cost-breakdown-1Mtokens.xlsx to the thread).
- Define success criteria (p95 <= 120ms, effective cost <= $400 per 1M tokens, cache hit >= 30%).
- Draft a short runbook for experiment orchestration (who runs seeds, how long per sweep).

I’ll join the kickoff to walk the cost model.

-Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering
ben.carter@redwoodelabs.com
